description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple memory allocation simulator. The module should take an input signal representing a request for memory allocation and an input signal indicating the size of the allocation. The module should also accept a free signal to deallocate a specified memory block. The output should indicate whether the allocation was successful or if the requested memory was already allocated or not available.
code:
module memory_allocator (
    input wire [3:0] request_size, // Size of the request (0-15)
    input wire allocate,            // Signal to allocate memory
    input wire free,               // Signal to free memory
    output reg success              // Allocation success flag
);

    reg [15:0] memory; // Simple memory simulation (16 bits)

    always @(*) begin
        success = 0; // Default success is 'false'

        if (allocate) begin
            // Check if the requested size is available
            if (memory[request_size] == 0) begin
                memory[request_size] = 1; // Mark as allocated
                success = 1; // Allocation successful
            end
        end else if (free) begin
            // Free the allocated memory block
            if (memory[request_size] == 1) begin
                memory[request_size] = 0; // Mark as free
                success = 1; // Free successful
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module bellman_ford(input [255:0] graph, // 16x16 adjacency matrix  
                    input [3:0] source, // source vertex (0-15)  
                    output reg [15:0] distance // shortest distances  
                   );  
    integer i, j, k;  
    parameter NUM_VERTICES = 16;  
    reg [15:0] dist [0:NUM_VERTICES-1]; // distances array  
    initial begin  
        // Initialize distances  
        for (i = 0; i < NUM_VERTICES; i = i + 1) begin  
            dist[i] = 16'hFFFF; // Set to infinity  
        end  
        dist[source] = 16'h0000; // Distance to source is 0  
        // Bellman-Ford algorithm  
        for (k = 0; k < NUM_VERTICES - 1; k = k + 1) begin  
            for (i = 0; i < NUM_VERTICES; i = i + 1) begin  
                for (j = 0; j < NUM_VERTICES; j = j + 1) begin  
                    if (graph[i*16+j] != 0) begin // If there is an edge  
                        if (dist[i] + graph[i*16+j] < dist[j]) begin  
                            dist[j] = dist[i] + graph[i*16+j];  
                        end  
                    end  
                end  
            end  
        end  
    end  
    always @* begin  
        for (i = 0; i < NUM_VERTICES; i = i + 1) begin  
            distance[i] = dist[i];  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

code:
module cordic(clk, reset, angle, sine, cosine);
    input clk, reset;
    input [15:0] angle; // 16-bit input angle in radians
    output reg [15:0] sine, cosine; // 16-bit output for sine and cosine

    reg [15:0] x, y, z; // x and y for coordinates, z for angle
    reg [15:0] atan_table [0:15]; // Lookup table for arctangent values

    integer i;

    initial begin
        // Initialize the atan_table for CORDIC
        atan_table[0] = 16'h2000; // atan(2^-0) in fixed-point
        atan_table[1] = 16'h199A; // atan(2^-1)
        atan_table[2] = 16'h1333; // atan(2^-2)
        atan_table[3] = 16'h0D60; // atan(2^-3)
        atan_table[4] = 16'h0A3D; // atan(2^-4)
        atan_table[5] = 16'h052E; // atan(2^-5)
        atan_table[6] = 16'h0266; // atan(2^-6)
        atan_table[7] = 16'h0139; // atan(2^-7)
        atan_table[8] = 16'h009A; // atan(2^-8)
        atan_table[9] = 16'h004E; // atan(2^-9)
        atan_table[10] = 16'h0027; // atan(2^-10)
        atan_table[11] = 16'h0013; // atan(2^-11)
        atan_table[12] = 16'h0009; // atan(2^-12)
        atan_table[13] = 16'h0004; // atan(2^-13)
        atan_table[14] = 16'h0002; // atan(2^-14)
        atan_table[15] = 16'h0001; // atan(2^-15)
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x <= 16'h2000; // Initial x value (1.0 in fixed-point)
            y <= 16'h0000; // Initial y value (0.0 in fixed-point)
            z <= angle; // Load angle
            sine <= 16'h0000;
            cosine <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            x <= 16'h2000; // Reset x
            y <= 16'h0000; // Reset y
            z <= angle; // Reset z
            for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                if (z < 0) begin
                    // Rotation in the negative direction
                    x <= x + (y >> i);
                    y <= y - (x >> i);
                    z <= z + atan_table[i];
                end else begin
                    // Rotation in the positive direction
                    x <= x - (y >> i);
                    y <= y + (x >> i);
                    z <= z - atan_table[i];
                end
            end
            sine <= y;
            cosine <= x;
        end
    end
endmodule

module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] measurement, // Noisy sensor measurement
    input [15:0] control,     // Control input
    output reg [15:0] estimate // Estimated state output
);
    reg [15:0] x; // State estimate
    reg [15:0] p; // Estimate covariance
    reg [15:0] q; // Process noise covariance
    reg [15:0] r; // Measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] k; // Kalman gain

    // Initialize parameters
    initial begin
        x = 16'd0;
        p = 16'd1;
        q = 16'd1; // Process noise
        r = 16'd1; // Measurement noise
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            x <= 16'd0;
            p <= 16'd1;
        end else begin
            // Prediction update
            p <= p + q; // Update covariance

            // Measurement update
            k <= p / (p + r); // Kalman gain
            x <= x + k * (measurement - x); // Update state estimate
            p <= (1 - k) * p; // Update covariance
            
            estimate <= x; // Output the estimated state
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple I2C master controller that can send a start condition, transmit data, and send a stop condition. The controller should have the following inputs: `clk` (clock), `start` (trigger to begin transmission), `data_in` (8-bit data to transmit), and the outputs should be `SDA` (data line), `SCL` (clock line), and `ack` (acknowledge signal). The controller should operate in such a way that upon receiving the `start` signal, it sends the `data_in` followed by the `stop` condition, while generating the correct SCL clock signals.
code:
module i2c_master(
    input wire clk,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg SDA,
    output reg SCL,
    output reg ack
);
    reg [3:0] state; // State machine state
    reg [3:0] bit_cnt; // Bit counter
    reg [7:0] data_reg; // Register to hold the data

    localparam IDLE = 0, START = 1, TRANSMIT = 2, STOP = 3;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                SDA <= 1; // Idle state SDA high
                SCL <= 1; // Idle state SCL high
                ack <= 0; // No acknowledge initially
                if (start) begin
                    data_reg <= data_in; // Load data
                    state <= START; // Move to START state
                end
            end
            START: begin
                SDA <= 0; // Start condition
                SCL <= 1; // Keep SCL high
                state <= TRANSMIT; // Move to TRANSMIT state
                bit_cnt <= 0; // Reset bit counter
            end
            TRANSMIT: begin
                if (bit_cnt < 8) begin
                    SCL <= 0; // SCL low for data transmission
                    SDA <= data_reg[7 - bit_cnt]; // Transmit bit
                    bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1; // Increment bit counter
                    SCL <= 1; // SCL high for acknowledge
                end else begin
                    ack <= 1; // Data transmitted, set acknowledge
                    state <= STOP; // Move to STOP state
                end
            end
            STOP: begin
                SDA <= 0; // SDA low to begin stop condition
                SCL <= 1; // SCL high
                SDA <= 1; // SDA high to finish stop condition
                state <= IDLE; // Return to IDLE state
            end
        endcase
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg SCK,
    output reg MOSI,
    output reg CS,
    output reg done
);

    reg [2:0] bit_cnt;
    reg [7:0] data_buf;

    localparam IDLE = 3'd0,
               START = 3'd1,
               TRANSFER = 3'd2,
               STOP = 3'd3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            SCK <= 0;
            MOSI <= 0;
            CS <= 1;
            done <= 0;
            state <= IDLE;
            bit_cnt <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    CS <= 1;
                    done <= 0;
                    if (start) begin
                        CS <= 0; // Activate chip select
                        data_buf <= data_in;
                        state <= START;
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    SCK <= 0;
                    bit_cnt <= 7; // Start with the most significant bit
                    state <= TRANSFER;
                end
                TRANSFER: begin
                    MOSI <= data_buf[bit_cnt]; // Send data bit
                    SCK <= 1; // Clock high
                    #5; // Wait for half a clock period
                    SCK <= 0; // Clock low
                    if (bit_cnt == 0) begin
                        state <= STOP; // All bits transmitted
                    end else begin
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt - 1; // Move to next bit
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    CS <= 1; // Deactivate chip select
                    done <= 1; // Indicate transmission is done
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

- `pop`: Signal to indicate a pop operation
- `data_in`: Input data to be pushed onto the stack
- `data_out`: Output data from the top of the stack when popping
- `full`: Flag indicating if the stack is full
- `empty`: Flag indicating if the stack is empty

module LIFO_Stack (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input push,
    input pop,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg full,
    output reg empty
);
    reg [7:0] stack [0:7]; // Stack array of size 8
    reg [2:0] top; // Points to the top of the stack

    initial begin
        top = 3'b111; // Stack is empty
        full = 1'b0; 
        empty = 1'b1;
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            top <= 3'b111; // Reset the stack
            full <= 1'b0; 
            empty <= 1'b1;
        end else begin
            if (push && !full) begin
                top <= top + 1; // Increment top
                stack[top] <= data_in; // Push data
                empty <= 1'b0; // Stack is not empty
                if (top == 3'b111) full <= 1'b1; // Check if stack is full
            end

            if (pop && !empty) begin
                data_out <= stack[top]; // Pop data
                top <= top - 1; // Decrement top
                full <= 1'b0; // Stack is not full
                if (top == 3'b111) empty <= 1'b1; // Check if stack is empty

endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a CORDIC algorithm for calculating the sine and cosine of a given angle. The angle will be provided in fixed-point format, and the output should be the sine and cosine values also in fixed-point format. The module should have input registers for the angle and control signals to start the computation and reset the state.
code:
module cordic (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input [15:0] angle,  // Fixed-point representation of angle
    output reg [15:0] sin_out,  // Fixed-point sine output
    output reg [15:0] cos_out,  // Fixed-point cosine output
    output reg ready
);
    reg [15:0] x;  // Initial value for x (cos(0))
    reg [15:0] y;  // Initial value for y (sin(0))
    reg [15:0] z;  // Angle accumulator
    reg [3:0] iter;  // Iteration counter

    // CORDIC constants
    reg [15:0] atan_table [0:15]; // Lookup table for arctangent values

    initial begin
        // Initialize atan_table with fixed-point values
        atan_table[0] = 16'h3C90; // atan(2^-0)
        atan_table[1] = 16'h3C40; // atan(2^-1)
        atan_table[2] = 16'h3C20; // atan(2^-2)
        atan_table[3] = 16'h3C10; // atan(2^-3)
        atan_table[4] = 16'h3C08; // atan(2^-4)
        atan_table[5] = 16'h3C04; // atan(2^-5)
        atan_table[6] = 16'h3C02; // atan(2^-6)
        atan_table[7] = 16'h3C01; // atan(2^-7)
        atan_table[8] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-8)
        atan_table[9] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-9)
        atan_table[10] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-10)
        atan_table[11] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-11)
        atan_table[12] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-12)
        atan_table[13] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-13)
        atan_table[14] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-14)
        atan_table[15] = 16'h3C00; // atan(2^-15)
    end

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            x <= 16'h4000; // Initial value for cosine (1.0)
            y <= 16'h0000; // Initial value for sine (0.0)
            z <= 0; // Angle accumulator
            iter <= 0;
            ready <= 0;
            sin_out <= 0;
            cos_out <= 0;
        end else if (start) begin
            if (iter < 16) begin
                if (z < 0) begin
                    x <= x + (y >> iter); // x = x + y * 2^-i
                    y <= y - (x >> iter); // y = y - x * 2^-i
                    z <= z + atan_table[iter]; // z = z + atan(i)
                end else begin
                    x <= x - (y >> iter); // x = x - y * 2^-i
                    y <= y + (x >> iter); // y = y + x * 2^-i
                    z <= z - atan_table[iter]; // z = z - atan(i)
                end
                iter <= iter + 1;
            end else begin
                sin_out <= y;
                cos_out <= x;
                ready <= 1; // Computation is done
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input int_req_low,

);

description: Design an interrupt controller that manages two types of interrupts: external and timer interrupts. );

Design a combinational logic circuit that performs LU decomposition on a 2x2 matrix. The input will be a 2x2 matrix represented as four 4-bit binary values. The output should be two 2x2 matrices L and U, both represented as four 4-bit binary values. The lower triangular matrix L should have 1s on the diagonal, and U should be an upper triangular matrix.
code:
module lu_decomposition (
    input [3:0] a11, a12,
    input [3:0] a21, a22,
    output reg [3:0] l11, l12,
    output reg [3:0] l21, l22,
    output reg [3:0] u11, u12,
    output reg [3:0] u21, u22
);
    always @(*) begin
        // LU decomposition steps
        l11 = 4'b0001; // Lower triangular matrix L, l11 is always 1
        l12 = 4'b0000; // Lower triangular matrix L, l12 is calculated
        l21 = a21 / a11; // Calculate l21
        l22 = 4'b0001; // l22 is always 1

        u11 = a11; // Upper triangular matrix U
        u12 = a12; // Upper triangular matrix U
        u21 = 4'b0000; // u21 is always 0
        u22 = a22 - (l21 * u12); // Calculate u22
    end
endmodule

    input wire Clk,

);

description: Design a simple 2-bit branch predictor that uses a 2-bit saturating counter. The predictor has two states: strongly taken, weakly taken, weakly not taken, and strongly not taken. The input signal is a branch instruction, which will either be taken (1) or not taken (0). The output will indicate the prediction (1 for taken, 0 for not taken) based on the current state of the predictor.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_taken,
    output reg prediction
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    // State Encoding
    localparam ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN = 2'b11,
               ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN = 2'b10,
               ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN = 2'b01,
               ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN = 2'b00;

    // Update state based on branch outcome
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Reset state
            prediction <= 0; // Default prediction
        end else begin
            case (state)
                ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN; // Move to weakly taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end
                end
                ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN; // Move to strongly taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to weakly not taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end
                end
                ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN; // Move to weakly taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to strongly not taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end
                end
                ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to weakly not taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end else begin
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end

- From TRANSMITTING to COMPLETE on a signal `done`.
- From COMPLETE to IDLE on a reset signal `reset`.
The controller should also maintain a data register that holds the current data being transmitted.

module pcie_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire done,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] data_out,
    output reg state // 0: IDLE, 1: TRANSMITTING, 2: COMPLETE
);
    parameter IDLE = 0, TRANSMITTING = 1, COMPLETE = 2;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            data_out <= 16'b0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= TRANSMITTING;
                        data_out <= data_in;
                    end
                end
                TRANSMITTING: begin
                    if (done) begin
                        state <= COMPLETE;
                    end
                end
                COMPLETE: begin
                    // Wait for the next start signal
                    state <= IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule
